fixes.explanation: He ends with, "And bless me also." (Exodus 12:32) Think about that. Back in Exodus 5:2 Pharaoh said, "I do not know the LORD," and now he's asking Moses and Aaron for a blessing as he sends them off. That's quite a turn.

Verse 37 says the Israelites journeyed from Rameses to Succoth. The text adds about 600,000 men on foot, besides women and children. That's a LOT of people on the move, and I bet somebody in that crowd was already asking, "Are we there yet?"
It's actually False. Verse 39 says the people "…had not prepared any provisions for themselves." So no, nothing was prepared ahead of time. That's a batch with no timer set and no warning.

Verse 39 says, "For when they had been driven out of Egypt, they could not delay…" Think about the morning you're running late and you leave with one shoe and half a plan. Now make that a whole nation. I've baked under pressure, but nobody handed me a deadline like that. The rush is why the provisions never got prepared.
